security_audit.summary: All four static matches are false positives involving numeric input sanitization or a responsive-layout bullet, not system reconnaissance. The guide has separate high-risk privacy and prompt-injection concerns because customer data enters AI connectors and influences fraud decisions. These examples need data protections and independent fraud controls.

remediation.issue: AI fraud examples disclose customer contact and address data without privacy safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Minimize or redact personal data, document consent and retention requirements, and require an approved provider configuration before transmission.

remediation.issue: Untrusted checkout fields can manipulate free-form AI fraud classifications.
remediation.suggestion: Use deterministic fraud controls, strict structured outputs, isolated untrusted fields, and human review. Do not exempt all authenticated users.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line converts a posted product identifier to an integer after a nonce check. It performs no host, network, or environment reconnaissance.
The line sanitizes an inventory ability input with absint before a product lookup. The surrounding ability requires WooCommerce management permission.
The line sanitizes an order identifier before a WooCommerce order lookup. It does not collect system information or inspect the execution environment.
This is a documentation bullet naming the responsive grid block. It contains no executable behavior or reconnaissance instruction.

semantic_findings.title: Customer Data Shared With AI Providers
semantic_findings.description: Fraud examples send billing email, shipping address, phone, and address data to an AI connector without consent, minimization, or retention guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly place customer contact and address fields into prompts submitted through an AI connector. No privacy safeguard accompanies either transmission.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Can Bypass Fraud Classification
semantic_findings.description: Customer-controlled order fields enter AI prompts, while free-form model output directly determines suspicion or checkout warnings without strict validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompts interpolate customer-controlled fields and trust substring matches from free-form responses. The checkout example also exempts every authenticated user.

content.value_statement: WooCommerce projects require coordinated setup, payments, shipping, customization, testing, and optimization. This skill provides a phased workflow with WordPress 7.0 examples and practical quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Guides WooCommerce store setup, tax, currency, products, and attributes.
Structures payment integrations for Stripe, PayPal, offline methods, and checkout testing.
Defines shipping zones, rates, carrier integration, and AI-assisted recommendations.
Provides PHP examples for product content, customer questions, inventory updates, and order processing.
Covers optimization and testing with quality gates for storefront and WordPress 7.0 features.
limitations: Provides reference workflows and snippets, but does not install, configure, or deploy a store automatically.
Requires environment-specific validation for WordPress, WooCommerce, plugins, themes, hosting, and provider APIs.
AI fraud and checkout examples are demonstrations and are insufficient for production risk decisions.
Payment, privacy, tax, and shipping requirements still need qualified review for each market.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Store
use_cases.description: Create a phased launch plan covering catalog, tax, currency, payments, shipping, design, optimization, and acceptance checks.

use_cases.title: Implement Store Features
use_cases.description: Use focused examples for product content, customer questions, inventory abilities, order processing, and checkout validation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Client Delivery
use_cases.description: Apply repeatable phases and quality gates across WooCommerce builds while documenting environment-specific decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Store Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased checklist for a WooCommerce store selling [product type] in [country]. Include products, tax, currency, and launch checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Payment Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Stripe and PayPal integration for [store]. Include configuration, test cases, failure states, refunds, webhooks, and production validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Shipping Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Design WooCommerce shipping for [regions] using [methods]. Define zones, rates, free-shipping rules, carrier needs, and checkout tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review Advanced Abilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WooCommerce customization and propose secure WordPress 7.0 Abilities API handlers. Address permissions, validation, privacy, failures, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: Plan a WooCommerce launch for a domestic clothing store.
output: Setup: confirm hosting, currency, tax rules, customer accounts, and required plugins.
Catalog: define categories, attributes, variable products, images, inventory, and product validation.
Launch: test payments, shipping, email, mobile checkout, performance, backups, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Define checkout tests for Stripe and PayPal.
output: Verify successful, declined, canceled, duplicated, and interrupted payments in each provider sandbox.
Confirm webhook signatures, order status transitions, refunds, customer notices, and administrator alerts.
Repeat critical tests on mobile and after enabling caching.

output_examples.output: The review identifies personal-data exposure, prompt-injection risk, weak response parsing, missing fallback controls, and required human escalation.

best_practices: Validate every snippet against installed WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP, theme, and extension versions.
Use staging, sandbox gateways, test orders, backups, and rollback plans before production changes.
Apply least privilege, input validation, output escaping, privacy review, and deterministic controls around AI features.
anti_patterns: Do not copy demonstration snippets directly into production without security and compatibility review.
Do not send customer data to AI providers without minimization, consent, and documented retention controls.
Do not let free-form AI responses approve payments, classify fraud, or change orders without independent validation.

faq.question: Does this skill install WooCommerce?
faq.answer: No. It provides a development workflow, examples, prompts, and quality gates for an existing WordPress environment.

faq.question: Which payment gateways does it cover?
faq.answer: It outlines Stripe, PayPal, and offline payment setup, with testing guidance for checkout flows.

faq.question: Does it include shipping guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers zones, methods, flat rates, free shipping, carrier integration, and checkout validation.

faq.question: Are the AI fraud examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. They require privacy safeguards, prompt-injection defenses, deterministic fraud signals, strict response validation, and human review.

faq.question: What WordPress 7.0 topics are included?
faq.answer: The guide discusses AI connectors, DataViews, collaboration, admin changes, performance features, and the Abilities API.

faq.question: What should be tested before launch?
faq.answer: Test products, checkout, payments, shipping, email, mobile behavior, performance, AI features, DataViews, backups, and rollback procedures.
